slides: Tangents to a circle. It's a short lesson, but its two rules come up in the exam all the time.

slides.say: A tangent is a straight line that just brushes past the circle. It touches the circle at one point only.
at: A tangent is a straight line
It touches the circle at one point

slides.say: If the line were a little further in, it would go through the circle and cut it at two points. Then the part inside the circle would be a chord.
And if the line passed outside, it wouldn't touch the circle at all. It's just a line.
at: And if the line passed outside

slides.say: So our tangent only brushes the circle, at one point. This point is called the point of tangency.
Now a very, very important rule. The radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency.
at: Now a very, very important rule

slides.say: Here the tangent touches the circle at D. When I draw a radius to the point of tangency, from O to D, I get a ninety-degree angle between the radius and the tangent.
It doesn't matter where the tangent touches. Here, and here, the radius to the point of tangency is always perpendicular to the tangent.
This rule is used very often in the exam. So every time you see a circle question with tangents, don't think too much. Draw the radius to the point of tangency, and you get a right angle.
